title: Answer to Question: Regarding the Cyprus Affair
text:
Answer to Question: Regarding the Cyprus Affair

Question:

On 3/3/2012 the Minister for European Union Affairs in the Turkish government and chief negotiator, Egemen Bağış, made a statement to the correspondent of the newspaper "Kıbrıs" while on his visit to Britain to meet its officials about the Cyprus affair, saying: "All options are on the table for the solution in Cyprus. Just as the solution could be in the form of a union (a united state) by agreement between the two leaders, it could be in the form of two states (within a state) by an agreement on a settlement made between the two leaders, and it could be by annexing Northern Cyprus to Turkey. All options are on the table. But what we hope for, and what is on our minds, is that there be a union of two states in one state in Cyprus." However, the Turkish minister did not mention the original solution, which is the annexation of the whole of Cyprus to Turkey, for it was a part of it. So what is the reality of these statements? May Allah reward you with good.

Answer:

1- The Turkish minister put forward the old American projects, since America had put forward these plans of its own since the seventies of the last century: either the island is divided into two separate states, or the two sectors are like two states in one state, that is, a federal or confederal union, or the north of Cyprus is annexed to Turkey and its south to Greece.

However, now that the south of Cyprus has become a member state of the European Union, it is unlikely that there will be any thought of annexing the southern sector to Greece. Like Greece, it enjoys full membership of the Union, it has its independence, and consideration is given to it, as it will hold the rotating presidency of the European Union next July. The conditions of Greece are bad, especially the economic ones, so the people in the south do not favour joining it, even if they have Greek nationalist sentiments mixed with religious fanaticism.

Thus the Turkish threat comes from one side. This is the first time a Turkish official has uttered it since the Cyprus issue first appeared in reality, that is, since America began in the fifties of the last century to carry out actions in Cyprus in order to affect Britain's influence there and consequently expel it from there and take its place. Eventually Britain was compelled to give formal independence to Cyprus in 1960, and it installed over it a Christian man of religion, Archbishop Makarios, and made its agent Rauf Denktaş, as representative of the Muslims, his deputy. In this way the island remained united in Britain's grip.

It appears that the Turkish threat came after the stalling of the talks relating to Cyprus with the British, since Minister Egemen Bağış added in his statements to that newspaper on 3/3/2012, at his meeting with the British Foreign Secretary William Hague, saying: "Britain is watching the two sides sensitively, but I do not see it moving with great enthusiasm with regard to using its influence. We have worked to persuade it on this subject. Since Britain is one of the guarantor states in Cyprus, we believe that it must pursue a more effective policy and play a constructive role more strongly."

2- From this it appears that the British do not want the solutions that America puts forward, which the Turkish minister has put forward anew, even if they pretend that they support a solution to the issue. They, that is the British, have two important military bases in Cyprus containing more than 24 thousand British soldiers, besides eavesdropping and intelligence apparatus for spying on the region and monitoring it. It is one of the guarantor states according to the agreement signed in 1964, whereby it, Turkey and Greece are guarantor states of the situation that it drew up on the island after the events that the Greek Cypriots carried out against the Turkish Muslims. In this way Britain preserved its presence and influence there according to this agreement.

The southern sector of Cyprus is recognised internationally and by Europe, and it is part of the European Union, and Britain is part of the European Union, so the British presence in Cyprus has become as though it were an internal presence and not an external one, and the other states of the European Union are not troubled by this presence. Rather, they support the British position implicitly, even if they declared their support for the Annan Plan, because it secures the Greeks' control of government on the island and ends the existence of a Turkish state on it. Therefore Britain will not give up its presence and influence in Cyprus.

3- The Europeans exert pressure on Turkey to achieve demands of theirs under the name of the Cyprus file, which is one of the files that have not been settled between them and it and then closed. This is among the files pending in the face of Turkey's accession to the European Union, the number of these files being about 35, among them internal matters such as the subject of the so-called minorities, from the Kurdish file to the Alevi file to the Armenian file, to the file of democracy and human rights, to the file of amending the constitution and accepting international supervision of elections, and what relates to reducing the role of the military in government, and other files.

Among their demands relating to the Cyprus file is the opening of Turkish ports and airports to the Greek Cypriots. However, Turkey did not implement the agreement relating to that, because the Europeans did not fulfil their pledge to lift the embargo they impose on the Turkish Cypriots according to the agreement made between the two sides. So the Cyprus file, with seven other files, is frozen and has not been settled. Likewise Turkey refuses to recognise the state of Southern Cyprus that the Greeks control until the issue is settled. Britain worked through its agents to obstruct the American plan, which was called the plan of Kofi Annan, the former Secretary of the United Nations, when the majority in the southern sector of the island voted against it in 2004.

The Turks in the northern sector voted for it, at a time when the government of the northern sector under the presidency of Mehmet Ali Talat was an agent of America. Erdogan's government supported it strongly and put all its weight behind the vote for this plan. Rauf Denktaş strongly opposed it at the time and called for its rejection; indeed, he came to Turkey and complained about Erdogan's government to the Turkish military leadership, which opposed this government and at that time did not support the Annan Plan. This brought out the struggle between the agents of the English and the Americans in Turkey and in Northern Cyprus. This plan stipulated the unification of the island with the participation of the Turks in government in certain proportions, on condition that the Greek Cypriots have the larger share in government, and that the Turks cede part of their lands to the Greeks, in the proportion of 7%.

4- America will not accept that the issue be solved by annexing the north of the island to Turkey, with its southern sector then remaining as it is and the English remaining comfortable in it there. For if that happened and their presence and influence there were not touched, the English would be comfortable and accept it. But America will not accept that until it removes the influence of the English and takes its place, removes their bases and encamps there, since for more than fifty years it has been struggling with them there; so it will not accept extending its influence only in the north of the island and leaving the English comfortable in its south! The English, through their media, used to propose to America that it establish bases of its own in the northern part of the island, but the Americans did not undertake this step, because in it there is an acknowledgement of the English presence there. America put forward the Annan Plan in order to control both halves, by creating a new political formula on the island that enables it to control the government and compel it to carry out its orders.

5- The Turkish minister's statement on the option of annexing Northern Cyprus to Turkey, even if it is one of the old American projects, currently appears as a threat used as a pressure card against the British, the Europeans and the Greek Cypriots, because the British are comfortable with their situation in Cyprus and therefore do not show enthusiasm for solving this issue, and they obstruct the American projects through their agents on the island. The Turkish minister declared that from inside Britain, and directed the blame directly at Britain, which obstructs the solution, saying that it does not move with great enthusiasm with regard to using its influence, does not pursue a more effective policy and does not play a constructive role more strongly. These formulations are diplomatic, but they are an implicit accusation against Britain that it obstructs the solution, and indeed does not work for the solution.

Annexing Northern Cyprus to Turkey would increase the obstruction of Turkey's accession to the European Union, since the Europeans do not accept that. Therefore it is unlikely that Turkey will undertake that at the present time, as it is seeking to enter the European Union, and America supports it in this endeavour and puts pressure on the Europeans to meet its request, in order to achieve aims of its own against the European Union. At the same time it does not achieve for America what it aspires to, namely removing Britain's presence and influence from the island, because it would keep the situation of Southern Cyprus as it is, and America cannot penetrate it in this way. Accordingly, the Turkish minister's words are no more than a pressure card.

This is with the knowledge that annexing the north of the island is not difficult for Turkey, because it is considered to be under its control, since there are more than 30 thousand of its soldiers there, and the current leadership of the Turkish army has come to back the government and stand in its ranks. So this action would not anger the army and would preserve its presence there. The protection of the northern sector, its security and its interests are all tied to Turkey, and no one other than it recognises the state of this sector and its government, so its fate is in Turkey's hand. Annexing it would be the easiest thing possible, but the regime in Turkey is not independent; it revolves in America's orbit, and so it will not undertake this step except at its prompting. Thus the brandishing of the annexation of Northern Cyprus to it is in order to put pressure on the English and on the Greeks in Cyprus so that they accept the American plans.

6- The features of this matter will become clearer after next July, when the regime in the southern part of Cyprus takes over the rotating presidency of the European Union and the difficulty of Turkey's dealings with this Union appears. The Turkish minister Bağış, responsible for relations with the Europeans and their chief negotiator, declared to the aforementioned Cypriot newspaper, saying: "We will not address the regime of the Rum in Southern Cyprus when it takes over the rotating presidency of the European Union in July.... But we will deal with the Union as though we do not see the regime of the Rum as president of the Union.. The regime of the Rum in Southern Cyprus is behaving recklessly. And there is a possibility that we will not take part in the meetings in Brussels under the presidency of this regime." That is, the situation will be exploited, and this is an opportunity for America to create confusion and apprehension among the Europeans and the Greeks over that, if the English and their agents in the southern part of Cyprus do not make concessions and accept the American plan called the Annan Plan. The American Secretary of State Hillary Clinton affirmed that last year after her meeting with her Turkish counterpart Davutoğlu, saying: "We do not believe that the existing situation in Cyprus is in anyone's interest. We want to see a union of two zones and two communities (in Cyprus), and we want to see it as soon as possible" (16/7/2011 AFP). That is, America is not satisfied with the situation in Cyprus and wants to make it according to its vision.

7- As for the correct solution to the problem of Cyprus that Islam commands, it is that all of it be annexed to Turkey. Cyprus is an Islamic land, and it must be joined to its origin, Turkey. The island of Cyprus is an Islamic island that the Muslims opened in the era of our master Uthman, the third Rightly Guided Khaleefah. The European Crusaders occupied it in their first Crusades that they waged against the Islamic lands, but the Muslims later liberated it and returned it to its origin, the lands of the Muslims. It came under the rule of the Ottoman State like the rest of the lands of the Muslims, because the Khilafah passed to them. The English declared their control over it in the First World War and declared its annexation to Britain, and their agent Mustafa Kemal acknowledged that in the Treaty of Lausanne. Nevertheless, the Muslims in Turkey consider Cyprus a part of their lands, and they worked to support their brothers there in the sixties and in the seventies when they were subjected to massacres at the hands of the Rum, with the support of Britain and America by various means. And their army is still there to protect more than 300 thousand Muslims.

With all of the above, the project of annexing the northern sector of Cyprus to Turkey without the southern sector, in response to the American projects, even if it is unlikely and Turkey is not actually working to achieve it, is considered a concession of two thirds of the island to the Rum, that is, to the Kuffar; for the Turks, officially, popularly and in the media, apply these names to the Greeks in Cyprus, saying: the Rum, the southern Rum sector and the regime of the Rum. Contenting oneself with a third of the island, which is the northern part, is a contravention of Islam, and everyone who agrees to it bears its sin, because the original position is the annexation of the whole island of Cyprus to Turkey and joining it to its origin.

The government headed by Erdogan and his party is working to lose this issue finally and to change the Muslims' view of it, until their view of it becomes not that it is an island of theirs! The Kuwaiti agency KUNA reported from the Turkish newspaper "Akşam" on 9/3/2012 that a responsible source in the ruling Justice and Development Party said: "Erdogan's government believes that the Annan peace plan can form an important ground for achieving a lasting and just peace in Cyprus, especially since the United States and all the states of the European Union support this plan." He added: "The Justice and Development Party is seeking to establish a new view of the Cyprus question and to persuade many circles in Turkey not to look at this issue as a purely Turkish national issue; rather, it must be looked at on the basis that it is a human rights issue in the first place, and what concerns us in this matter is the protection of the rights of the Turkish Cypriots through American and European international guarantees."

Looking at Cyprus as a human rights issue, like any foreign issue in the far corners of the earth, and not as the issue of an Islamic land separated from its origin, this view in this manner is a loss of Cyprus, and everyone who contributed to this loss or was content with it bears the sin of it until the Day of Resurrection. The Muslims will not give up Cyprus, nor any part of the lands of the Muslims that the oppressive rulers have lost; rather, they will restore it, by the permission of Allah, if not sooner then later, and tomorrow is near for the one who watches for it.
